messages:
jordan: quick follow-up to the console authz RFC — proposing we split authorization out of the synchronous query hot path. high-level goal: reduce p99/p999 for dashboard panels without weakening safety. sketch below.

maya: +1. we've been seeing p99 spikes on tenant-heavy dashboards. need something incremental. :eyes:

alex: to quantify — during last loadtest auth checks added ~120ms p99 when fanout > 30 (mostly cross-AZ RPCs). that's expensive.

ravi: idea: async preflight service that materializes compact allow bitmaps (or route allow lists) per tenant & policy_version. runtime consults local cache first and only falls back to sync check on miss.

taylor: main concern is revocation/staleness. how do we guarantee immediate denies (compliance)?

jordan: plan: two-pronged. (1) short TTLs for sensitive perms (10s), longer for stable perms (5m). (2) invalidation hooks: when policy changes or revokes happen we push invalidation events to preflight cache and runtimes. for high-sensitivity routes, runtime also does a sync deny-check on every request (configurable).

maya: can we colocate a read-only replica of policy store near the runtime (edge) to avoid cross-AZ calls? reduces tail.

alex: yes, local replica helps, but consistency windows increase. must be explicit in SLOs.

jordan: interface sketch for the preflight API (very small):

```
Authorize(tenant_id, subject, route_ids[]) -> { allowed_map: {route_id: bool}, cache_ttl_s: int, policy_version: string, reason_map: {route_id: string} }
```

alex: also include a "known_denies" list for batch prefiltering to avoid extra roundtrips.

ravi: implementation detail: preflight responses should include policy_version so runtime can tag cache entries and invalidate when version mismatch.

taylor: rollout & safety: cache must be conservative. default on cache-miss should be sync-check -> DENY if sync-check says deny. we should never allow-by-default.

jordan: agreed. cache semantics: only cache explicit allows (and maybe explicit denies with short TTL). on unknown -> sync. We'll run read-through first, then only-if-stable convert to authoritative cache.

maya: metrics we need: per-route cache_hit_rate, cache_miss_rate, auth_sync_latency(p50/p95/p99), auth_fallback_rate, and broken-down token-level cost delta. add a small tracing tag to correlate token cost with auth path.

alex: rollout proposal: week0 instrument + feature flag plumbing. week1 canary 5% tenants (read-through only). week2 20%. week3 all read-through. week4 enable cache-authoritative for low-risk routes (fanout < 10).

ravi: security note: signed cache entries HMACed between preflight and runtimes, rotated keys via KMS. include nonce/timestamp to mitigate replay.

taylor: SLO tradeoffs: we can reduce p99 for panels by ~30-60% in heavy cases but add operational complexity. need a runbook for stale policies and a fast invalidate path.

jordan: action items — @maya own canary, @alex implement preflight client + signing, @ravi wire invalidation hooks and policy_versioning, @taylor author SLOs & alerts, i'll draft the rollout playbook and put canary gates in CD.

maya: on it. I'll start a checklist in the runbook doc.

alex: will start a small lib for Authorize calls (go + rust bindings). expect a PR by EOW.

ravi: I'll prototype invalidation via pub/sub (redis streams or kinesis) and load test.

taylor: i'll write the alerting thresholds: fallback_rate > 1% or auth_sync_p99 > 200ms triggers pager.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: authz-preflight:v1 -> canary(5%) scheduled @ 2026-04-02T03:00Z

jordan: thanks folks — this keeps console latency goals realistic without rebuilding the whole query layer. we can iterate on the policy model later.

maya: :thumbsup: any objections before I own the canary?

alex: none from me. small note: ensure telemetry tags include "policy_version" and "auth_path" (cache|sync|fallback).

ravi: agree. also add a quick log line for cache-miss reasons to make debugs less painful.

taylor: dropping here. i'll add SLO doc link once drafted.

jordan: closing for now, will follow up with the rollout playbook PR.
